threats.title: Mechanically Versatile Soft Machines through Laminar Jamming
threats.reason_investigated: Foundational direct layer-jamming prior art; tests whether the full residual act collapses to ordinary layer-jamming modeling/experiment.

threats.mechanism_overlap: High: Coulomb interlayer friction and slip transition.
threats.model_overlap: Moderate: Euler-Bernoulli/friction model, not Zhang-type homogenized continuum M1.

threats.operating_domain_overlap: Vacuum pressure and layer count overlap; finite tested range.
threats.what_it_proves: Laminar jamming beams exhibit pressure-dependent variable stiffness governed by Coulomb friction. | Pre-slip bending stiffness scales with layer count cubed (or N^2 relative to unjammed). | Euler-Bernoulli beam theory with friction slip captures the qualitative transition loads.
threats.what_it_does_not_prove: Does not prove validity for high layer counts (N > 25); explicitly states single-crystal homogenization as open future work. | Does not quantify output-specific model-form error boundaries across a systematic (N x p_vac x kappa) domain. | Does not formulate a homogenized continuum beam governing differential equation.
